says: In next/, the law 'P2: runners select policy before init and retain policy, pending recovery and counts on reopen' runs 100 cases of up to 100 commands on real runners, and once took more than 4 times its usual time and hit the 60 s limit.
proof: It timed out at 60 s once, in https://github.com/kamp-us/tea-fabrika/actions/runs/43334569348/job/131588023241 (attempt 1 on the t883-wire-flake branch, `Error: Test timed out in 60000ms.`), and the rerun of that same run went green. In the CI logs of 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-14 it took 11.5 to 13.7 s in the runs that passed. The instance-records saved-waits scenario timed out in the same job at the same moment, so the cause may be that job's runner and not this law's work: the read of the law found no wall-clock wait in it.
cost: A run that is about 4 times slower than usual turns this law red with no bug, now on the 3-hour schedule.
